title: bug: switching approvalMode on the board neither cancels nor arms SPEED auto-approval timers, so a plan armed under SPEED is still auto-approved seconds after the human switches to CONTROL, and plans pending when the human switches to SPEED wait until the next daemon restart
description:
Filed by defect hunt #12 (task-f6f0b580, architect-1dd28c7c). Reproduced at moe/work-2026-10-24 f159784e; the files are unchanged at cbae6070.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/):
- The only settings write path is /ws UPDATE_SETTINGS (server/WebSocketServer.ts:828-833) → StateManager.updateSettings (StateManager.ts:1308) → updateProjectSettings (state/profileRollout.ts:140). That function validates, writes and emits, but never touches the SPEED timers.
- Under SPEED, submit_plan arms a per-task timer (tools/submitPlan.ts armSpeedModeApproval, :114-155).
  - The timer re-checks only that the task is still AWAITING_APPROVAL (:127-128), then writes WORKING with PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED.
  - It never re-reads approvalMode.
- The twin rule: under CONTROL, set_task_status refuses AWAITING_APPROVAL→WORKING ("requires human approval in CONTROL mode", setTaskStatus.ts:151-162). An armed timer bypasses that gate for up to speedModeDelayMs (default 2000 ms) after the human switches to CONTROL.
- The reverse direction: rearmSpeedModeApprovals (submitPlan.ts:170) runs only at startup (index.ts:842).
  - AWAITING_APPROVAL rows that are pending when the human switches CONTROL→SPEED are never armed.
  - They all approve at once after the next daemon restart.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md:190-191 describes SPEED as "auto after delay". Nothing in the docs says a mode switch applies to new submissions only.

EVIDENCE:
- /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/B/zzHuntB_speedModeSwitch.test.ts uses zzHuntB_harness.ts: a real StateManager, McpAdapter and MoeWebSocketServer, a JetBrains-shaped UPDATE_SETTINGS { approvalMode: 'CONTROL', … } and speedModeDelayMs 400. Run in a git-archive snapshot of f159784e: Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2).
  - ✓ twin rule: under CONTROL, set_task_status refuses AWAITING_APPROVAL -> WORKING
  - × a plan armed under SPEED is NOT auto-approved after the board switches the project to CONTROL → AssertionError: expected 'WORKING' to be 'AWAITING_APPROVAL'. A PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED event is logged.
- My re-run: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/me/me-zzHuntB_speedModeSwitch.log
- Plugin reach: the JetBrains MoeSettingsDialog approval-mode combo (MoeCommandSender.kt:80-89, UPDATE_SETTINGS) and the VS Code SettingsPanel (MoeDaemonClient UPDATE_SETTINGS).
- Exposure: this project runs TURBO, which arms no timers. SPEED users are the ones affected.

FIX DIRECTION: after a successful settings write that changes approvalMode:
- becoming CONTROL → call clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts();
- becoming SPEED → call rearmSpeedModeApprovals(state). It is already idempotent: it skips armed rows and non-SPEED projects.
- TURBO can keep armed timers, since it approves anyway.
Both functions are exported from tools/submitPlan.ts. Import them; do not edit submitPlan.ts, which task dd1e00f8 holds. Put the calls in updateProjectSettings (profileRollout.ts) so every settings path gets them. If the state→tools import is unwanted, put them in WebSocketServer.ts's UPDATE_SETTINGS case instead, a hunk distinct from the update_epic row's UPDATE_EPIC case.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/profileRollout.ts (or the UPDATE_SETTINGS case of packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts), and a new test such as src/state/approvalModeSwitch.test.ts. docs/CONFIGURATION.md's approvalMode row may gain one sentence. No docs/MCP_SERVER.md change is needed.
definitionOfDone: A plan armed under SPEED is not auto-approved when approvalMode changes to CONTROL before its timer fires: it stays AWAITING_APPROVAL and no PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED event is logged (fake timers or a short speedModeDelayMs).
An AWAITING_APPROVAL row pending when approvalMode changes to SPEED is auto-approved after speedModeDelayMs without a daemon restart, and a row that is already armed is not armed twice.
A new vitest file covers both directions and passes, and the existing submit_plan SPEED-mode tests stay green.

implementationPlan.note: Added the post-write approvalMode switch hook in updateProjectSettings (CONTROL -> clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts, SPEED -> rearmSpeedModeApprovals, TURBO/unchanged -> nothing) and a new 7-case approvalModeSwitch.test.ts. Red first in a git-archive snapshot: with the hook absent s1 (SPEED->CONTROL) and s2 (CONTROL->SPEED) failed and the 5 guard cases passed; with it, 7/7 pass and tsc --noEmit is clean.

implementationPlan.description:
Docs. Follow governor ruling msg-71db57ac: sync your own section. No other open row edits these two places. Edit with your own editor (Claude Edit, or apply_patch on codex). Never use Serena, which ignores docs/, and never a shell write. Work in your task checkout.
(1) docs/MCP_SERVER.md, section `### Plan approval — expectedPlanRevision compare-and-swap`. Directly after the `- **Restart re-arm.** …` bullet under **SPEED/TURBO auto-approval.**, add this bullet:
- **Mode switch.** The timers also follow `approvalMode` changes (the board's `UPDATE_SETTINGS`, `StateManager.updateSettings`). A switch to `CONTROL` cancels every armed SPEED timer, so nothing armed under SPEED is approved after the human asked for manual approval. A switch to `SPEED` arms every `AWAITING_APPROVAL` row by the restart re-arm rule above: bound to its submitted revision, the remaining delay counted from `planSubmittedAt`, and rows already armed skipped. A switch to `TURBO` leaves armed timers running.
(2) docs/CONFIGURATION.md, `### SPEED Mode` list. Add after the 'bound to the revision' bullet:
- Switching `approvalMode` to `CONTROL` cancels pending SPEED auto-approvals; switching to `SPEED` arms every plan already awaiting approval, as a daemon restart does
Touch nothing else in either file.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of your diff (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD "${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-HEAD}")`). Expect roughly +150/-0 across profileRollout.ts, the new test and the two docs. For each item, check it and fix what fails, then for error handling confirm (1) and (2) below.
(1) The hook runs only after a successful write. A validation refusal or a write failure (atomicWriteJsonAsync throws) must neither clear nor arm.
(2) Neither call can throw past the write. rearmSpeedModeApprovals records failures per row; confirm no new throw path was added.
(3) Concurrency: updateSettings runs under the state mutex (/ws withMutex). armSpeedModeApproval detaches the timer from the mutex context (submitPlan.ts:119-123), so the timer's runExclusive still locks.
(4) A mode that is undefined on either side is treated as CONTROL, so no hook fires for an omitted key.
(5) clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts empties the map, so a later re-arm rebuilds it cleanly. A timer that already fired and is waiting on the mutex re-checks the status only, so a switch landing in that window can still approve one row. Note this residual race in the completion summary: it needs a submitPlan.ts change, and dd1e00f8 holds that file.
(6) The tests use fake timers with advanceTimersByTimeAsync, restore real timers in afterEach, and assert exact outcomes: the status, the count of PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED events, and approvedPlanRevision.
(7) Nothing outside updateProjectSettings, the new test and the two doc places changed.
If anything changes, re-run the step-3 command and submit that fresh output.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Changing approvalMode through updateSettings, the only settings write and the one the board's UPDATE_SETTINGS uses, now reaches the in-memory SPEED timers. Switching to CONTROL cancels every armed timer, so no plan armed under SPEED is auto-approved after the switch. Switching to SPEED arms every AWAITING_APPROVAL row by the daemon-start re-arm rule. Switching to TURBO leaves armed timers running. MCP_SERVER.md's Plan approval section and CONFIGURATION.md's SPEED Mode list document the switch.
acceptanceCriteria: SPEED then CONTROL before the timer fires: the row stays AWAITING_APPROVAL with no PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED event.
CONTROL then SPEED with a pending row: the row is approved after speedModeDelayMs with no restart, with exactly one PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED event bound to its submitted revision.
Already-armed rows are not re-armed, and a settings write that leaves the mode unchanged does not touch the timers.
Existing SPEED-mode, profileRollout, StateManager and WebSocketServer tests stay green.
invariants: A refused or failed settings write never clears or arms a timer.
There is at most one live SPEED timer per task. armSpeedModeApproval cancels the prior timer, and rearm skips armed rows.
compatibility: The settings wire shape, validation and SETTINGS_UPDATED emit are unchanged. Only the post-write timer side effect is new.
submitPlan.ts is not edited, because dd1e00f8 holds it. The hook uses only its existing exports.
Restart behavior is unchanged: index.ts:842 still re-arms at start.

tools/submitPlan.ts armSpeedModeApproval (:114-155): the timer re-checks only status === 'AWAITING_APPROVAL' (:127-128) before writing WORKING with PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED.

tools/submitPlan.ts:170 rearmSpeedModeApprovals returns unless state.project.settings.approvalMode === 'SPEED'. It skips rows already in speedModeTimeouts and computes remaining = max(0, delay - (now - planSubmittedAt)).
Under CONTROL, setTaskStatus.ts:151-162 refuses AWAITING_APPROVAL to WORKING. That is the twin rule the armed timer bypasses.
